Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to the Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call of SBI 
Funds Management Limited. From the management team, we have: Mr. Debasish Mishra, 
Managing Director and CEO; Mr. Srinivas Jain, Joint CEO; Mr. Manish Mehta, Chief Business 
Officer; Mr. Amol Joshi, Chief Financial Officer; Vinaya Datar, Chief Compliance Officer; 
Dinesh Balachandran, Head of Investments; Manish Chheda, Chief Investor Relations Officer, 
joining the call. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Debasish Mishra. Thank you, and over 
to you, sir. 
Debasish Mishra: 
A very good evening to everyone and thank you for taking the time to join the call. Let me begin 
with a brief view of the macro environment. The second quarter was marked by steady domestic 
fundamentals and broadly stable earnings, even as global pressures from higher crude, firm US 
yields, and a stronger dollar triggered foreign outflows and bouts of volatility. Despite this, 
strong domestic participation helped absorb the outflow shock, reflecting the ongoing shift of 
household savings into financial assets and keeping overall market sentiment resilient.  
Now, I will brief about the mutual fund industry. Mutual fund quarterly average AUM expanded 
by 13% year-on-year and 5% sequentially as on 30th September 2026, touching INR 87.5 trillion 
at the end of September 30. Monthly SIP inflows continued to show strength despite market 
volatility and touched all-time record high of INR 32,490 crores in September'26. On fixed 
income, debt AUM saw a 5% year-on-year moderation, while liquid AUM recorded a strong 
27% increase. Passive AUM grew 23% year-on-year, highlighting sustained investor interest.  
Overall, industry inflows remained constructive despite short-term volatility across all 
categories. Industry continued to have a positive new customer addition, reaching up to 6.3 
crores unique customers, an increase of 11% year-on-year.  
Now, let me tell you the performance of SBI Funds Management. The company sustained its 
leadership in the industry, with quarterly average AUM market share of 15%. Our mutual fund 
quarterly average AUM stood at INR 13.14 lakh crores, registering 10% Y-o-Y growth 
compared to INR 12 lakh crores in the same quarter last year. As on September 30, 2026, our 
active quarterly average AUM was INR 8.99 lakh crores, reflecting 9% year-on-year increase, 
and our 5-year CAGR was 17%, backed by stable performance and sustained investor flows.  
On passive front, we remain the largest passive asset manager with quarterly average AUM of 
INR 4.15 lakh crore, up by 11% year-on-year, further strengthening our leadership in that 
segment. On the alternate side, PMS and advisory QAAUM stood at INR 13.32 lakh crore, 
broadly in line with expectations. While the previous quarter saw a one-time relocation of a large 
mandate, it doesn't have any material impact on our revenues, and the underlying business 
momentum remains stable.  
Our AIF platform continues to scale well, with QAAUM at INR 7,437 crores, reflecting 27% 
year-on-year growth. To further strengthen and deepen our AIF capabilities, we have also added 
a dedicated business head for the AIF practice, bringing sharper focus to product expansion and 
institutional engagement. Offshore funds contributed approximately INR 42,100 crores to the 
overall AUM. Gross margins across equity, debt, liquid, and passive strategies remained stable 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
              
 
Page 3 of 12 
 
during the quarter, and there has been a continued expansion in gross yields on a year-on-year 
basis.  
Our unique customer count increased by 10% during the year, rising to 1.85 crores as of 
September 30, 2026. Our SIP AUM rose to INR 2.07 lakh crores with a 15% year-on-year 
increase. Monthly SIP inflows continue to remain steady at about INR 3,900 crores. We continue 
to maintain one of the largest distribution networks in the industry, supported by nearly 136,000 
distribution partners. This includes over 125,000 independent financial advisors, over 10,000 
national distributors, and over 96 banking partners, including State Bank of India, supplemented 
by 23,000+ SBI branches and 297 SBI Funds Management branches. This extensive reach 
enables us to service investors across more than 98% of pin codes in the country. 
Our strong presence across Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities is reflected in the healthy B-30 contribution, 
with nearly 2/3rd of SIP inflows originating from these markets, underscoring our expanding 
reach and commitment to broad-based financial inclusion.  
Let me brief you about the new product launches. We continue to maintain a strong product 
pipeline across Mutual fund, SIF, PMS, and AIF, with a clear emphasis on differentiated, 
investor-focused offerings. During Q2, we launched five new products, including one SIF, 
further strengthening our overall product suite. Among the filed offerings, both the Magnum 
Equity Ex‑Top 100 Long Short Fund, and SBI Balanced Hybrid Fund saw stronger investor 
responses. Our Magnum Equity Ex-Top 100 Long Short Fund closed its NFO as one of the 
largest funds in its category.  
Our GIFT City franchise continues to scale well, supported by the launch of SBI Global 
Thematic Advantage Fund. This initiative enables the investors in India to access global 
investment opportunities through LRS route. We are enhancing our capabilities across active, 
passive, and alternative strategies, with strong traction in AIF, PMS, and SIF, and growing 
international reach through GIFT City and offshore mandates, reinforcing our ability to serve 
rising India-focused demand.  
Now, I'll brief you about technology and digital improvements. We continue to strengthen our 
digital-first approach. Today, 94% of our transactions are done digitally, supported by stronger 
adoption across InvesTap, Mitra, and partner platforms. InvesTap has grown into one of the 
largest digital investing apps in the industry, with over 4.3 million registered users. Monthly 
digital volumes now exceed 1.4 million transactions, and our ongoing investment in technology, 
AI, and automation are helping us to scale efficiently, enhance distributor productivity, and 
deliver seamless experience to investors.  
We recently showcased our new tech platform called Aarambh at the Global Fintech Festival in 
Mumbai. Aarambh is one of the first assisted digital onboarding solutions built specifically for 
first-time investors. It enables Aadhaar-based biometric KYC, folio creation, and first 
investment in a single seamless journey. Importantly, it helps us to reach customer segments that 
remain outside the formal financial ecosystem, strengthening our financial inclusion efforts. 
Aarambh also integrates digital PEKRN i.e. PAN-exempt KYC reference number for customers

without a PAN card, allowing us to extend mutual fund access to the masses in a simple and 
compliant manner.  
Coming back to financial performance, for H1 FY27, operating revenue reached to INR 2,336 
crores, up to 12% from INR 2,089 crores in the same period last year. Operating profit rose to 
INR 1,797 crores, compared to INR 1,626 crores in H1 FY26, an 11% increase. Profit after tax 
came in at INR 1,566 crores in H1 FY27. Our strong net-worth of INR 7,270 crores as on 
September 30, 2026, continues to support strategic investment in scale, capabilities, and long-
term value creation.  
To conclude, our strategy will focus on four key pillars: democratizing wealth creation, 
accelerating digital delivery, strengthening investment performance, and building new growth 
engines. With this clear agenda, we aim to deliver consistent outcomes for our investors and 
continue to build a strong, technology-driven, and future-ready franchise.  
Thank you for joining the call. We now look forward to your questions.

in Q2, which will not be repeated in the Q3.
